text:
alex: quick FYI — after yesterday's kernel-selection tweak i see a spike in OOMs and some latency blips on the long-tail when batch packing hits 8+ sequences on the rtx-60 fleet. digging in now, but wanted to flag before we roll more of v3 kernels.

maria: ugh — numbers?

alex: summary: OOM rate up ~12% on p50 traffic windows, p99 latency +30ms on batch sizes >=8, and alloc stalls in the logs around logits/scratchpad growth. nvprof traces point to big transient allocations during decode step.

perf-bot: profiling link: https://perf.internal/runs/1861234567 (contains heap timeline + kernel events)

jyoti: can you paste the heap timeline snippet? curious if this is freelist churn or a real fragmentation issue.

alex: snippet from the capture:
```
[ALLOC] step=decode token=42 size=3.2MB -> device_malloc (no free bucket)
[FREE] step=decode token=42 size=3.2MB -> freed to device_freelist (size class 4MB)
[ALLOC] step=decode token=43 size=3.2MB -> device_malloc (freelist empty due to eviction)
[OOM] step=decode token=44 -> failed alloc 6.4MB
```

alex: looks like our eviction policy for the pooled buffers is too aggressive when KV cache pages are pinned concurrently; freelist gets drained during heavy beam/streaming workloads.

sam: hypothesis: logits buffers and scratchpads have different lifetime profiles than activation tensors. we should isolate pools per-lifetime class so long-lived kv pages don't evict transient buffers.

maria: Agreed. Also we should ensure workspace sizing for convolution kernels uses worst-case per-batch compute instead of naive per-request formula — that's causing oversized temporary allocs in some codepaths.

jyoti: proposal: multi-tier pool with small/medium/large buckets + LRU eviction tuned by "last_touch" and a soft memory cap. keep a dedicated pinned pool for KV pages (never evict unless >X% used) and allow transient pool to borrow but with fast fallback to host staging.

alex: config prototype I sketched:
```yaml
pool:
  tiers: 3
  size_classes_bytes: [16384, 65536, 262144, 1048576, 4194304]
  max_per_class: 128
  soft_evict_after_seconds: 30
  pinned_kv_threshold_pct: 40  # won't evict pinned pool unless >40% used
  transient_borrow_limit_pct: 20
```

sam: nice. also add an option to reuse logits buffers across steps when beam search reuses shapes — that saves a malloc/free cycle per token. we can mark logits as "sticky" for N steps.

maria: +1. telemetry we need: alloc_count_by_class, evict_count, failed_allocs, time_to_alloc, and per-step mem delta. tag experiments with `pool_reuse_v2` in traces.

perf-bot: canary checklist generated: canary 2% traffic, run for 24h, collect p50/p95/p99 latency, oom_count, evict_rate, and mem_trace.

jyoti: I'll implement the allocator changes and the sticky logits option. plan: staged rollout — unit tests -> perf canary -> 50% -> full. estimate 3 days for initial impl + 1 day for canary.

alex: thanks. one more: add a guard to fallback to quantized-kernel path if transient alloc fails instead of throwing OOM at decode time. should reduce customer-visible failures.

sam: i'll add the kernel-fallback hook in the routing layer. default off for now.

maria: assign owners? jyoti (allocator + eviction), sam (kernel fallback + telemetry), alex (canary + metrics dashboards). i'll coordinate the rollout and postmortem if needed.

alex: sweet. starting branch `allocator/multi-tier-reuse` now. ping me for review. :thumbsup:

sam: can we also capture a microbenchmark for logits reuse vs fresh alloc (tokens/sec delta)? i'll add a jenkins job.

jyoti: noted. will include in PR.

maria: thanks team. if perf-bot sees regressions during canary it should auto-rollback.

perf-bot: will monitor and alert on oom_count>3 in 10m window.

alex: any objections to this plan?

maria: none. go ahead.

sam: go for it.

jyoti: will post the PR link when ready.
